subject.title: fix(hooks): bound hook workspace manifest and HOOK.md reads

question: Should workspace hook package.json and HOOK.md files above 1 MiB be rejected with a warning as the permanent core compatibility policy?
rationale: The implementation is sound, but selecting the byte ceiling intentionally changes which previously readable workspace hooks load after upgrade; repository evidence cannot establish the desired product boundary.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Land the current warn-and-skip policy because these files are metadata, exact-limit inputs remain supported, and oversized failures are actionable rather than fatal.

options.title: Choose a larger fixed ceiling
options.body: Raise the shared constants before merge if maintainers know legitimate workspace hook documentation or manifests can exceed 1 MiB.

options.title: Preserve unbounded compatibility
options.body: Decline the cap and retain current behavior, accepting the existing memory-exhaustion exposure during workspace discovery.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Land the current warn-and-skip policy because these files are metadata, exact-limit inputs remain supported, and oversized failures are actionable rather than fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, this account is the best available authority for accepting a new core compatibility boundary.
